findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the plan (co-located with the G3 rubric update description) the decision rule for what constitutes 'covers it' when matching a parent AC against a sibling's roster AC text snippet — e.g., whether the full three-part coverage standard applies, or a looser semantic-equivalence rule is used for the cross-check gate.
evidence: Current plan_review_G3.md defines THREE-PART COVERAGE STANDARD for full-plan evaluation; the plan does not say whether this standard applies to roster AC snippets.
The plan says 'the roster's acceptance criteria' are used to discharge the anti-false-positive rule, but gives no rule for what level of AC-text match constitutes 'covers it'.
A text snippet like '- [ ] The widget renders in under 200ms' may partially match a parent AC about performance — no protocol says whether partial is sufficient for the cross-check.
The plan explicitly says G3's posture/threshold are 'deliberately left untouched' but says nothing about the coverage-matching rule for snippet-level roster entries.
findings.finding: The plan says G3's rubric must instruct the reviewer to test 'no sibling covers it' against the roster's acceptance criteria (the new indented AC text items). However, the plan never co-locates a decision rule for what 'covers' means at the AC-text-snippet level — the existing G3 rubric (plan_review_G3.md) defines a THREE-PART COVERAGE STANDARD (SAME OBSERVABLE OUTCOME / scope MATCHING-OR-EXCEEDING / measurable IN THE SAME TERMS) that applies when a full child plan is under review, but the roster now carries only extracted AC items, not full child descriptions. The plan does not specify whether this three-part standard applies to snippet matching, or a simpler semantic-equivalence rule applies, leaving the G3 rubric update under-specified for the instruction the LLM must follow.
findings.location: Approach section, '(2) Make G3's child-coverage audit able to fire' / `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` rubric update; AC line: 'G3's rubric instructs the reviewer to test "no sibling covers it" against the roster's acceptance criteria'
scenarios: Two different G3 rubric authors write incompatible matching rules — one uses the full three-part standard (very hard to satisfy from a snippet), another uses loose semantic match (easy to satisfy) — producing inconsistent false-positive suppression.
The LLM applies the three-part standard to a roster AC snippet, cannot confirm 'scope MATCHING-OR-EXCEEDING' from a snippet, and always fires the finding anyway — defeating the fix.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Describe the exact mechanism by which the rendered roster reaches `passes.pass1_container` after removal from `instructions` — either (a) specify the new parameter `pass1_container` gains and confirm all three call sites are updated accordingly, or (b) show that `passes.py` can receive the roster without importing from `pass1.py` (e.g., `pass1.py` builds the roster and passes it through an existing dict or new parameter without a reverse import).
evidence: 'build_sibling_roster emits one block per child…' — placed in pass1.py
'in passes.pass1_container, build the system prompt as _resolve_system(PASS_CONTAINER, parent_plan, cfg) concatenated with a rendered roster block' — placed in passes.py

ABSENCE: no description of (a) the new pass1_container parameter that would carry the roster string, (b) how pass1.py passes the roster to pass1_container without passes.py importing from pass1.py, or (c) any acknowledgement of the circular-import risk
findings.finding: The Approach places `build_sibling_roster` in `pass1.py` (which already imports from `passes.py`) and simultaneously says `passes.pass1_container` will concatenate the rendered roster into its system prompt — but never specifies how the rendered roster value travels from `pass1.py` into `passes.pass1_container` after being removed from `instructions`. Two resolutions are possible: (a) `passes.py` imports `build_sibling_roster` from `pass1.py`, which creates a circular import since `pass1.py` imports `passes`; (b) `pass1_container` gains a new explicit roster parameter, meaning all three listed callers must update their call sites — but neither the new signature nor the mechanism avoiding the circular import is described anywhere in the plan.
findings.location: Approach section — '(2) Make G3's child-coverage audit able to fire' / 'Where the roster is sent' subsection; cross-referenced with Scope listing for pass1.py and passes.py
scenarios: An implementer following the plan as written either creates a circular import (passes.py ← pass1.py ← passes.py) or silently changes pass1_container's call signature in a way that makes the three caller-update instructions incomplete, since the plan only tells callers to 'call the shared helper' but not how to forward the result to pass1_container.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `pass1.py` call `build_sibling_roster(children)` to obtain the rendered roster string, then pass it to `passes.pass1_container` as a new keyword argument (e.g., `roster_block`); `pass1_container` in `passes.py` concatenates `roster_block` to the system prompt. Update all three call sites accordingly. This keeps `passes.py` free of any import from `pass1.py` and resolves the ambiguity about where the string originates.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief design note (e.g., a comment block in `passes.py` near `pass1_container` and/or an entry in `AGENTS.md`) recording *why* the roster rides the system-prompt prefix rather than per-pairing instructions (caching boundary, O(n²) avoidance), so future contributors cannot inadvertently revert it without understanding the tradeoff.
evidence: Plan states the roster moves to the system prompt prefix to avoid O(n²) re-sends and enable caching, but no AGENTS.md / ADR / design-doc update appears in the Scope list.
The Testing section adds test_roster_rides_prefix_not_instructions to guard the regression, but a test guards correctness — it does not document the architectural rationale for future contributors.
The 'docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md' update covers the criterion catalog, not prompt-construction conventions.
findings.finding: The decision to move the sibling roster from per-pairing `instructions` into the system-prompt prefix is a non-trivial prompt-architecture decision — it establishes a convention about what belongs in the stable prefix vs. per-pairing payload for the container pass. No ADR, AGENTS.md entry, or design-doc update is listed in Scope to capture this pattern durably. A future contributor modifying `passes.pass1_container` has no durable record of why the roster lives in the prefix (caching boundary, avoiding O(n²) re-sends) and could accidentally revert the structure.
findings.location: Scope section / passes.py change / Approach ('Where the roster is sent')
scenarios: A contributor refactoring passes.pass1_container sees no architectural record explaining the prefix/instructions split and re-introduces the per-pairing roster, regressing caching and re-introducing O(n²) token cost.
A new pipeline stage added later repeats the pattern inconsistently because the convention was never written down.
findings.suggested_fix: In `passes.py`, add a module-level or function-level docstring/comment block explaining the prompt-structure invariant: 'The sibling roster is placed in the system-prompt prefix (not per-pairing instructions) to (a) avoid re-sending the full AC corpus once per child pairing — O(n²) token growth — and (b) make the roster eligible for prefix caching when the prefix clears CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS. Do not move it to instructions without re-evaluating both properties.' Optionally mirror a one-liner in AGENTS.md under prompt-construction conventions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the bundle is justified beyond test-fixture deduplication: if `build_sibling_roster` and `ac-satisfiability` have no structural runtime dependency on each other (only a shared test fixture in `pass1.py`), consider whether the fixture can be shared across two separate leaf tickets instead, allowing each concern to ship and be reviewed independently.
evidence: "They ship as one story because the second one's proving tests instantiate the container pass that the first one's registration also touches, so splitting them would duplicate that fixture"

The ac-satisfiability criterion (rubric file + routing entry + registry + single-turn chunk path) has no structural dependency on the roster changes; the only shared surface is pass1.py and a test fixture.
Both pieces have independent ACs, independent value, and independent test suites — nine ACs for criterion 1, seven for criterion 2 — suggesting they are independently releasable.
findings.finding: The plan bundles two independently-releasable outcomes — (1) a new `ac-satisfiability` criterion (rubric, routing, registry) and (2) G3 roster enrichment + `build_sibling_roster` refactor + `passes.py` system-prompt move — justifying the bundle solely on shared test fixtures in `pass1.py`. The two features serve different stakeholders (criterion reviewers vs. container-pass maintainers), have separate reasons to change, and would each deliver value independently. Shared fixtures are a test-organizational concern that can be resolved without coupling the deliverables.
findings.location: Approach section, paragraph beginning 'Two defects with two separate causes. They ship as one story because…'
scenarios: If the G3 roster work encounters unexpected complexity (e.g. passes.py LOC cap issues, eval_solver integration problems), it blocks the independently valuable ac-satisfiability criterion from shipping.
Reviewers of the combined ticket must reason about both pass1.py roster logic and LLM routing/rubric content simultaneously, increasing cognitive load and review error risk.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit `block_threshold` numeric value to the `ac-satisfiability` routing-entry specification (the plan currently names only `exec`, `facet`, and `default_posture`).
evidence: Plan says: 'The criterion ships `advisory` at the `0.95` default' — but this reads as prose rationale for choosing advisory, not as a specified field value.
Existing advisory entries in criteria_routing.json all carry explicit block_threshold: F4=0.95 (line 43), necessity, decomp-shape, asserted-capability.
_validate_routing_entry is called for every entry at registry.py:550-554; the AC for the routing entry omits block_threshold entirely.
The phrase 'the 0.95 default' implies a schema default that does not exist in the routing schema.
findings.finding: The plan states the `ac-satisfiability` criterion ships 'advisory at the 0.95 default' but never specifies a `block_threshold` numeric value for its `criteria_routing.json` entry. `validate_packaged_routing()` calls `_validate_routing_entry` on every entry (registry.py:550-554), and all existing advisory entries carry an explicit `block_threshold` (e.g., F4=0.95, decomp-shape, necessity, asserted-capability). There is no schema default for this field; an implementer cannot write a conforming routing entry from the plan alone.
findings.location: Scope / `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` routing entry for `ac-satisfiability`; also AC line: '`ac-satisfiability` is a registered plan-review criterion routed as `exec: "1-TURN"`, `facet: "coherence"`, `default_posture: "advisory"`'
scenarios: Implementer writes the routing entry without block_threshold → validate_packaged_routing() fails CI on the first run.
Implementer guesses 0.95 but that value is only inferred from prose, not specified — a different implementer may choose differently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `"block_threshold": 0.95` to the `ac-satisfiability` entry specification in the plan, matching the prose rationale already given ('the 0.95 default').

findings.finding: A third independent copy of the roster-building expression exists in `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:117-119` — outside `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — and is not enumerated in the Scope or Testing sections. findings.finding: The plan never specifies the rendered format of AC-bearing roster entries that `build_sibling_roster` will emit. The G3 rubric update is described only as instructing the reviewer to test against 'the roster's acceptance criteria', but the actual structure — how `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` items (raw checklist strings) are serialized per roster entry — is undefined. This is a processing-rule/schema co-location gap: the G3 rubric needs to know the format to correctly apply the anti-false-positive rule, and `build_sibling_roster`'s output contract is equally unspecified.
findings.location: Approach section ('Where the roster is sent' + 'Make G3's child-coverage audit able to fire'); Scope: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` (`build_sibling_roster` helper); `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md`
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section a concrete rendering spec for roster entries that carry AC items, e.g.: each entry is `'- {ticket_id}: {title}\n  acceptance criteria:\n{indented_ac_items}'` where `indented_ac_items` is each `ac_items` string prefixed with `'    '`. Mirror this exact format in the G3 rubric update so the reviewer instruction is format-aware.
